kind.rationale: One Sui-family instance per network (design section 1.2); no Sui code exists in the repo, so the ledger saga and accounting are reused by copy.

standard.rationale: Recommended for groundwork: Currency Standard (coin_registry), 8 decimals, unregulated, unknown-supply model; make_regulated is never called (irreversible).

signed_payload.value: BLAKE2b-256 digest of the intent prefix and the BCS transaction data, signed with Ed25519 (signature flag 0x00). The ICP mapping is an inference from two docs.

value.text: SUI for gas must be sent to the canister's Sui address from outside the canister.
Publishing the Move package needs gas and yields an UpgradeCap to the publisher.

open_decisions.topic: Sui: Move gate module or per-intent deposit addresses

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): plan the small Sui Move gate wrapping TreasuryCap, mint-id consumption, counters and recipient-bound returns; UpgradeCap stays a separate, disclosed authority; custody and live changes remain held.

open_decisions.topic: Testnet escrow: real icUSD ledger or a test ledger

choice.rationale: Design section 12 (settled for planning): synthetic test ledgers for future testnet demos; no real canonical icUSD is locked for a new testnet rollout under this groundwork.

activation_blockers.text: A plain coin transfer carries no ICP account, and a TreasuryCap mint keeps no consumed-id record. A Move gate module (consumed table, counters, BridgeOut event) is needed (D4). No Sui code exists in the repo.

JSON-RPC is disabled on Sui Foundation mainnet full nodes and the Foundation GraphQL endpoints are rate-limited and for development and testing only. A contracted GraphQL provider is needed for anything beyond a demo.

UpgradeCap stays a separate, disclosed authority (D4 planning decision), and it is a mint-path authority: make_immutable removes the fix path and a lost key strands the cap. Custody and any live change are held until D6 is decided.
No Sui wallet connector exists in the frontend; Slush is the main wallet named in the docs.
The controller and upgrade-authority model for this instance and its chain-side authorities is not decided (D6). The controller set is the root of trust for escrow and every signature.

value.typical_wait: not found in a primary source (transactions are final once in a finalized checkpoint, and checkpoints do not fork)

min_quorum.rationale: Baseline of 2 identical results. Only one Foundation GraphQL endpoint is documented per network, so a contracted provider is needed (blocker sui-rpc-provider-contract).

outcall_notes.value: GraphQL is an HTTPS POST of JSON, so it is the only Sui path that plainly fits HTTPS outcalls; JSON-RPC is being decommissioned and no official ICP canister exists for Sui. Foundation endpoints have strict rate limits.
